content:
maya: Heads-up — after the kernel + driver sweep this morning, a small subset of Dedicated nodes in ap-southeast1 are seeing repeated NCCL timeouts and occasional inference segfaults. Not wide yet but failures spike when batch size > 8.
ash: ugh. Symptoms/logs?
maya: paste from node-aps1-42: `E NCCL Timeout 10.25s; op=allReduce; rank=3; peer=5` then a python segfault from pytorch runtime.
tj: does it correlate with a specific driver version?
maya: yes, driver 535.86 + kernel 6.1 combo. older nodes on 535.54 are fine.
liam: that's the new vendor kernel patch we rolled last week. We tested on h100 canary but only with small batches.
serena: customers on Dedicated paying SLAs — we should avoid full region rollback if possible. Can we phase back the driver on only affected image pools?
maya: proposed plan: 1) freeze deploys to ap-southeast1; 2) shift traffic for Dedicated customers in that region to older machine image with driver 535.54 (repurpose warm pool); 3) run compatibility sweep on a 10-node canary with synthetic peak loads; 4) if stable, proceed with staged upgrade with health hooks.
nash: +1. How do we detect instability automatically?
tj: health hook idea — kernel-driver smoke that runs a short NCCL allreduce across local ranks and a short inference trace with batch sizes 1/8/16. Return non-zero on mismatch or segfault. We already have ops-bot able to run canned checks.
ops-bot: scheduled check launched on node-aps1-canary-007: `./ncc_test.sh --sizes 1,8,16 --retries 3`
liam: can we also prevent autoscaler from placing new Dedicated workloads onto nodes with driver 535.86 until sweep completes?
maya: yes — add a taint to the k8s node pool: `kubectl taint nodes node-aps1-* driver-sweep=blocked:NoSchedule` while canary runs.
serena: timeline constraints: customer churn risk if we shift capacity during EMEA business hours. Let's aim for rollback window in a low-traffic period for ap-southeast1 (UTC midnight window).
nash: need runbook snippets for rollback ops for on-call. Adding here: 1) cordon affected nodes, 2) drain workloads to warm pool, 3) bump machine image to driver 535.54 with `image-rollout --pool dedicated-aps1 --to v2026-02-14-driver53554`, 4) uncordon.
tj: include quick validation: curl to health endpoint on each node `/internal/driver-health` expecting `{"status":"ok","driver":"535.54"}` — if any fail, abort.
maya: sample commands posted in #eng-infra-docs. Also we should coordinate with sales and SRE to pre-announce potential brief hits.
liam: cost note — shifting traffic to warm pool increases burst costs ~12% for that region during the window. Serena ok with notifying finance for temporary overage.
serena: fine, we can absorb one-off. Prioritize avoiding escalations.
nash: do we want a short-term kernel shim to avoid NCCL timeouts? Vendor suggested an env var workaround: `NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1` but it masks root cause. Not ideal for prod.
tj: only use as last-resort canary step, and gate it behind canary flag.
maya: ok I'll create a phased rollout checklist and assign owners: canary run — @tj, traffic shift — @liam, rollback ops — @ash, customer comms — @serena.
ops-bot: created incident task INC-2026-089 and assigned owners: tj, liam, ash, serena.
maya: thanks — starting canary now. Will post initial results in ~10m.
ash: thanks, keep thread updated. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: canary results: 10m run completed, 0 NCCL timeouts at batch 1/8, 3 failures at batch 16 (repro). Marked canary unstable.
maya: canary unstable confirms need to rollback or limit batch sizes. Rolling forward is not safe.
liam: initiating traffic shift to warm pool and image rollback per runbook now.
serena: ping sales & support about brief capacity shuffle.
nash: once rollback done, let's schedule a deeper QA matrix with vendor on the kernel-driver combos and collect driver stack traces.
maya: rollback in progress — will update when complete.
ops-bot: rollback completed on 35 nodes. Post-rollback healthchecks green.
maya: rollback successful, no customer-facing errors observed in the last 15m. Opening postmortem doc and vendor escalation ticket.
serena: good work. Follow-up: plan a phased re-test with driver vendor patch and add the batch-16 test to our CI for Dedicated images.
nash: +1, also add an automatic metric alert for NCCL timeout rate > 0.5% per region.
tj: will draft CI test and kernel-driver matrix. End of thread for now.
